subtitle: Bhulabhai Desai and the Last Argument of an Empire

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Red Fort looming at dusk
panels.action: Bhulabhai Desai stands in his black gown before the massive walls of the Red Fort at dusk, his face calm yet intent, while ghostly silhouettes of INA soldiers and naval ratings seem to rise behind the battlements.

dialogue.text: In 1945, in the shadow of the Red Fort, Bhulabhai Desai turned a treason trial into a mirror — and the empire saw its own armies looking back in doubt.

i18n.hi: 1945 में, लाल क़िले की छाया में, भूलाभाई देसाई ने ग़द्दारी के मुक़दमे को आईना बना दिया — और साम्राज्य ने अपनी ही फ़ौजों को शक से झाँकते देखा।

panels.shot: wide aerial of war-torn Asia fading into Delhi
panels.action: A sweeping view shows battle-scarred landscapes of Southeast Asia dissolving into the domes and gates of Delhi’s Red Fort, guarded by British Indian soldiers in khaki.

dialogue.text: The Second World War had bled continents. In Asia, prisoners had chosen a different flag — Subhas Bose’s Azad Hind, the Indian National Army.

i18n.hi: दूसरे विश्वयुद्ध ने महाद्वीपों को लहूलुहान कर दिया था। एशिया में क़ैदियों ने दूसरा झंडा चुना — सुभाष बोस का आज़ाद हिंद, इंडियन नेशनल आर्मी।

panels.shot: medium interior of a modest study, lamplight
panels.action: In a simple Bombay study lit by a single lamp, Bhulabhai Desai, white-haired and bespectacled, leans over law books and files, his black gown folded neatly beside him.

dialogue.text: Far from the front, an aging barrister watched these storms. Bhulabhai Desai — veteran lawyer, Congress leader, believer in argument as weapon.

i18n.hi: मोर्चे से दूर, एक बूढ़ा बैरिस्टर ये तूफ़ान देख रहा था। भूलाभाई देसाई — पुराना वक़ील, कांग्रेस नेता, बहस को हथियार मानने वाला।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Desai reading a telegram
panels.action: Close on Bhulabhai Desai seated, brows furrowed, as he holds a telegram, its folded paper trembling slightly in his hand.

dialogue.text: In late 1945 a message came. Three INA officers would be tried by court-martial at the Red Fort — for waging war against the King.

i18n.hi: 1945 के आख़िर में ख़बर आई। तीन आईएनए अफ़सरों पर लाल क़िले में कोर्ट मार्शल होगा — बादशाह के ख़िलाफ़ जंग छेड़ने के लिए।

panels.shot: profile medium of Desai rising from his chair
panels.action: Bhulabhai Desai rises slowly from his chair, determination hardening his gentle features as he reaches for his black gown.

dialogue.speaker: bhulabhai_desai
dialogue.text: If law is their weapon, let us meet them in that arena.

i18n.hi: अगर क़ानून उनका हथियार है, तो हम भी उसी मैदान में उतरेंगे।

panels.shot: epic wide of Red Fort interior courtyard
panels.action: An interior courtyard of the Red Fort is filled with British officers, Indian soldiers, and journalists; Bhulabhai Desai walks in, robed, flanked by fellow Indian lawyers, towards a military courtroom.

dialogue.text: In November 1945, the fort that once housed emperors became a courtroom. Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon and Prem Sahgal now stood where Mughal power had once ruled.

i18n.hi: नवंबर 1945 में, कभी बादशाहों का महल रहा क़िला, अदालत बन गया। शाह नवाज़ ख़ान, गुरबख्श सिंह ढिल्लों और प्रेम सहगल वहीं खड़े थे जहाँ कभी मुग़ल ताक़त राज करती थी।

panels.shot: tight medium of Desai addressing the court
panels.action: Bhulabhai Desai stands at a simple lectern before a panel of British and Indian officers, his hand gently resting on a stack of documents, his gaze steady and intense.

dialogue.text: Desai chose not to plead for mercy. He challenged the foundation: if Azad Hind was a government, could obedience to it be treason?

i18n.hi: देसाई ने रहम की भीख नहीं माँगी। उसने नींव पर ही चोट की: अगर आज़ाद हिंद सरकार थी, तो उसकी बात मानना ग़द्दारी कैसे हुआ?

panels.shot: close-up on Desai’s face in mid-argument
panels.action: An intense close-up shows Bhulabhai Desai speaking, lips slightly parted, eyes bright, as officers listen in stony silence beyond the frame.

dialogue.speaker: bhulabhai_desai
dialogue.text: When a people seek their own sovereign, is loyalty to them a crime?

i18n.hi: जब लोग अपना हक़ीकी हकूमत माँगें, तो क्या उनकी वफ़ादारी जुर्म बन जाती है?

panels.shot: wide shot of crowded gallery and press benches
panels.action: A packed gallery of Indians in various regional dress craning forward, reporters scribbling, as Desai’s figure is visible at the distant centre of the courtroom.

dialogue.text: Outside the legal codes, another verdict was forming. Crowds followed every word. For many, the docked officers were not traitors — they were symbols.

i18n.hi: क़ानून की किताबों से बाहर, एक और फ़ैसला पक रहा था। भीड़ हर शब्द पर टिकी थी। बहुतों की नज़र में कटघरे के अफ़सर ग़द्दार नहीं — निशानियाँ थे।

panels.shot: muted montage-style wide: courtroom contrasted with streets
panels.action: Split composition: on one side the stern faces of the military judges inside the Red Fort; on the other, Delhi streets with posters of INA men and processions carrying flags.

dialogue.text: The court weighed charges of desertion and murder. On the streets, slogans spoke of sacrifice, Bose and freedom. Law and sentiment pulled in opposite directions.

i18n.hi: अदालत भगोड़ेपन और क़त्ल के इलज़ाम तौल रही थी। सड़कों पर नारे क़ुर्बानी, बोस और आज़ादी की बातें कर रहे थे। क़ानून और जज़्बात दोनों उल्टी दिशाओं में खिंच रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium of Desai seated, exhausted, as judgment is read
panels.action: Bhulabhai Desai sits motionless, shoulders slightly slumped, as distant military judges, barely visible, read out the conviction; INA officers stand erect beside him.

dialogue.text: In the end, the court-martial followed the book. The officers were found guilty, sentenced to transportation and dismissal from service.

i18n.hi: आख़िर में, कोर्ट मार्शल ने किताब के मुताबिक़ फ़ैसला दिया। अफ़सर मुज़रिम क़रार हुए, काला पानी और फ़ौज से बर्ख़ास्तगी की सज़ा मिली।

panels.shot: close-up on Desai’s hands clasped together
panels.action: Close on Bhulabhai Desai’s hands clasped tightly on his knee, veins visible, as faint chants drift in from outside through a barred window.

dialogue.text: On paper, Desai had lost. But the echo of his arguments carried beyond the Red Fort walls, into bazaars, mills and barracks.

i18n.hi: कागज़ पर देसाई हार गया। मगर उसकी दलीलों की गूँज लाल क़िले की दीवारों से निकलकर बाज़ारों, मिलों और बैरकों तक फैल गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of mass protest outside the Red Fort
panels.action: Huge crowds throng the streets outside the Red Fort, policemen forming a cordon as protesters raise placards and flags, faces tense and animated.

dialogue.text: Protests flared across cities. The government, watching the anger and unrest, commuted the sentences. The law’s judgment remained; its punishment softened under pressure.

i18n.hi: शहरों में जगह-जगह विरोध भड़के। सरकार ने ग़ुस्से और बेक़रारी को देख, सज़ाएँ हल्की कर दीं। फ़ैसला वही रहा; सज़ा दबाव में नरम पड़ गई।

panels.shot: map-like aerial transitioning from Delhi to port cities
panels.action: A stylised aerial view shows Delhi shrinking as the perspective sweeps towards the ports of Bombay, Karachi, and Calcutta, where silhouettes of ships cluster in harbours.

dialogue.text: But the deeper tremor lay elsewhere. In the very forces meant to guard the empire, discontent had been hardening into anger.

i18n.hi: पर असली हलचल कहीं और थी। ख़ुद साम्राज्य की रखवाली करने वाली फ़ौजों के भीतर, नाख़ुशी सख़्त होकर ग़ुस्से में बदल रही थी।

panels.shot: deck-level wide shot on a Royal Indian Navy ship in Bombay
panels.action: On the sunlit deck of a Royal Indian Navy ship in Bombay, young Indian ratings in blue uniforms stand in line, some weary, some whispering, with the city’s skyline hazy behind.

dialogue.text: In February 1946, ratings of the Royal Indian Navy — poorly fed, racially slighted, war-weary — watched the INA trials and the news with growing bitterness.

i18n.hi: फ़रवरी 1946 में, रॉयल इंडियन नेवी के नाविक — भूखे, नस्ली तौहीन झेलते, जंग से थके — आईएनए मुक़दमों और ख़बरों को बढ़ती तल्ख़ी से देख रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of ratings around a mess table
panels.action: A group of ratings sit around a simple mess table; one slams a metal mug down as others lean in, tense, a crumpled newspaper with INA headlines lying between them.

dialogue.text: Food complaints mixed with politics. The trials turned abstract grievances into a shared cause. On 18 February, a strike began in Bombay.

i18n.hi: खाने की शिकायतें सियासत से घुल गईं। मुक़दमों ने धुँधले ग़ुस्से को एक साझा मक़सद बना दिया। 18 फ़रवरी को बंबई में हड़ताल भड़क उठी।

panels.shot: dramatic wide of ships with flags and painted slogans
panels.action: Several warships in Bombay harbour are shown with sailors lining the rails; improvised flags and nationalist slogans are visible as painted banners along the hulls.

dialogue.text: Within days, it spread: 78 ships, 20 shore establishments from Bombay to Karachi and Calcutta. Ratings raised nationalist slogans and defied orders.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही दिनों में ये लौ फैल गई: 78 जहाज़, 20 नौसैनिक ठिकाने, बंबई से कराची और कलकत्ता तक। नाविकों ने राष्ट्रवादी नारे लगाए, हुक्मों को ठुकरा दिया।

panels.shot: street-level wide of Bombay crowd watching the harbour
panels.action: A teeming Bombay street near the waterfront, crowd pressed against barricades, watching distant ships while discussions and arguments break out among civilians.

dialogue.text: Onshore, responses split. Some political leaders hailed their courage; others worried at the chaos of an armed mutiny.

i18n.hi: तट पर जवाब बँट गए। कुछ नेता उनकी हिम्मत को सलाम कर रहे थे; कुछ सशस्त्र बग़ावत की अफ़रातफ़री से सहमे हुए थे।

panels.shot: interior medium of a nationalist leader in discussion
panels.action: Inside a modest office, an Indian political leader in traditional dress speaks earnestly to British officials, hands open in appeal, as documents lie spread on a table.

dialogue.text: Mahatma Gandhi opposed the uprising, fearing violence without discipline. Vallabhbhai Patel worked, step by step, to persuade the ratings to lay down arms.

i18n.hi: महात्मा गांधी ने बग़ावत का विरोध किया, उन्हें बिना अनुशासन वाली हिंसा का डर था। वल्लभभाई पटेल ने क़दम-दर-क़दम नाविकों को हथियार डालने को राज़ी करने की कोशिश की।

panels.shot: somber wide of armed British troops facing a ship
panels.action: Armed British and Indian troops line the quay, rifles held ready but lowered, facing a RIN ship whose decks are still crowded with ratings.

dialogue.text: The empire could not ignore armed defiance in its own fleet. Guns were brought up, ultimatums given. Behind every order lay the memory of other naval mutinies.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य अपनी ही बेड़े में हथियारबंद बग़ावत अनदेखी नहीं कर सकता था। तोपें तैनात हुईं, अल्टीमेटम दिए गए। हर हुक्म के पीछे पुरानी नौसैनिक बग़ावतों की यादें थीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of ratings lowering a flag
panels.action: On a ship’s deck, a young rating slowly lowers an improvised nationalist flag, his jaw clenched, as shipmates stand in a silent line beside him.

dialogue.text: After appeals from nationalist leaders and the threat of overwhelming force, the ratings surrendered between 22 and 23 February. Their demands unmet, their defiance recorded.

i18n.hi: कौमी नेताओं की अपीलों और भारी ताक़त के ख़तरे के बीच, 22 से 23 फ़रवरी के बीच नाविकों ने आत्मसमर्पण कर दिया। माँगें अधूरी रहीं, मगर उनका सिर उठाना दर्ज हो गया।

panels.shot: montage wide of courtrooms, ships, and crowds fading together
panels.action: A layered composition shows, fading into each other, the Red Fort courtroom, a naval dockyard with silent ships, and crowds of Indians filling city streets.

dialogue.text: Historians would later see these moments together — the INA trials, the naval revolt — as signs that the empire’s moral claim over its Indian soldiers was breaking.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकारों ने बाद में इन लम्हों को एक साथ देखा — आईएनए ट्रायल और नौसैनिक बग़ावत — बतौर निशानी कि भारतीय सिपाहियों पर साम्राज्य का नैतिक हक़ डगमगा रहा था।

panels.shot: quiet medium of an older Desai seated, reflective
panels.action: In a later moment, Bhulabhai Desai sits in an armchair, thinner and weary, gazing out of a window, INA trial files stacked neatly on a side table.

dialogue.text: Bhulabhai Desai did not live to see full independence. Yet his arguments echoed in every later debate on sovereignty, loyalty and the right to resist authority.

i18n.hi: भूलाभाई देसाई ज़िंदा रहते पूर्ण आज़ादी नहीं देख पाए। लेकिन उनकी दलील हर बाद की बहस में गूँजी — हकूमत, वफ़ादारी और हुक्म के ख़िलाफ़ बग़ावत के हक़ पर।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Desai’s silhouette against the Red Fort
panels.action: Silhouette of Bhulabhai Desai, seen from behind, stands alone facing the distant outline of the Red Fort at twilight, as the city lights of Delhi flicker to life.

dialogue.text: An empire weakens when those who guard it question its justice. In the Red Fort and on the seas, Bhulabhai Desai and the ratings forced that question into the open — where it still waits for every power.

i18n.hi: जब रखवाली करने वाले ही इंसाफ़ पर सवाल उठाएँ, तो साम्राज्य कमज़ोर पड़ जाता है। लाल क़िले की अदालत और समंदरों के जहाज़ों पर, भूलाभाई देसाई और नाविकों ने उस सवाल को खुली हवा में छोड़ दिया — जहाँ हर सत्ता को आज भी उसका जवाब देना है।

subtitle_i18n.hi: भूलाभाई देसाई और साम्राज्य की आख़िरी दलील
